attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is applied to every URL match, and URL_RE's `[^\s<>"]+` allows arbitrarily long punctuation runs inside one token. The anchored `+$` pattern is retried from each start position in the run, so work grows roughly quadratically with run length. Descriptions have no length cap, so an owner can store a very long token that stalls rendering for every neighbor who opens the item.

Nothing bounds description length before tokenize and truncate run. The expanded branch renders every token as a DOM node, so a very long description or one with thousands of links produces a large DOM on expand.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any maximum length for item.description. Expanded branch: `(expanded ? all : short.tokens).map(...)`

attacks.claim: Trailing ')' is stripped from every URL without checking for a matching '(' in the URL. Balanced-paren URLs such as Wikipedia article links are cut short, so the link points to the wrong page and the stripped ')' appears as plain text. The tests do not cover this case.

The PR says truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens so a word is never split. The fallback hard-cuts a text token mid-word when no whitespace is in range and nothing has been emitted yet. The behavior is deliberate and tested, but the stated invariant and the test title 'never splits a link or a word' overstate it.
attacks.evidence: "truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens, so a URL is never split" vs. "else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') });"

attacks.claim: The budget uses UTF-16 `.length` for the fit check, but the fallback slices by code points with Array.from. For text with emoji or other astral characters, the emitted text can exceed 280 UTF-16 units, so the limit is not reliable for non-BMP text.

ItemDescription keeps `expanded` state but has no `key`. If the same ItemPage instance is reused when switching items, the new description can inherit the previous item's expanded or collapsed state. Routing is not shown in the artifact, so this is conditional.
attacks.evidence: <ItemDescription text={item.description} /> with no key prop; const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);

attacks.claim: Link text is the raw URL in an unbroken inline anchor, and the diff adds no overflow-wrap or word-break rule. On narrow phones a long manual or product URL may overflow its container. Existing styles are not shown, so the severity depends on them.

attacks.claim: Links beyond the 280-character cut are hidden until the user taps 'Show more'. Owners paste manual and product links for borrowers, so the most useful content may be the most likely to be hidden.
attacks.evidence: expect(screen.queryByRole('link')).toBeNull(); (collapsed state, with the URL after the cut)

attacks.claim: Owner-authored arbitrary http(s) links are now clickable on the item page for every signed-in neighbor, with no domain display or warning. This adds a phishing surface. noopener, noreferrer and nofollow address tab-nabbing and referrer leakage, not this.
